items.a: No. AP2 moves no money and defines no fee. It carries signed evidence of what the user authorized on top of cards, bank transfers or stablecoins.

items.q: Is AP2 the same as A2A?
items.a: No. A2A (Agent2Agent) is one transport that the AP2 samples use. Version 0.2 describes AP2 as a security feature inside a commerce protocol and leaves the messages to that protocol, for example UCP.

items.q: Does AP2 v0.2 still have Intent and Cart Mandates?
items.a: No. Version 0.2 has only Checkout and Payment Mandates, each closed or open. Intent and Cart Mandates belong to v0.1, which most 2025 tutorials describe.
Not alone. Google donated AP2 to the FIDO Alliance on 2026-04-28, and specification work continues in FIDO's Payments Technical Working Group. Google keeps the samples and SDK.

items.q: Did FIDO create two new working groups for AP2?
items.a: Only one. The Agentic Authentication Technical Working Group was new on 2026-04-28; the payments group, chaired by Mastercard and Visa, has existed since 2025-04-29.

items.q: Is AP2 live in Gemini or in UCP?
items.a: Not verifiably. UCP specifies an AP2 extension and Google said in May 2026 it would bring AP2 to its products, but no primary source shows production use anywhere.

items.q: What is the difference between an open and a closed mandate?
items.a: A closed mandate binds to one checkout with exact values. An open mandate holds constraints and the agent's public key in cnf, so the agent can later sign a closed mandate inside those limits.

items.q: Can a user revoke an open mandate?
items.a: Not in v0.2. No revocation mechanism exists; the specification recommends the shortest expiry that lets the agent finish.
No. v0.2 specifies no step-up; a failed check falls back through unresolved_constraint. v0.1 allowed 3DS2 or OTP challenges, and the Executive Summary still mentions them.

items.q: Is the MPP in AP2 the Machine Payments Protocol from Stripe and Tempo?
items.a: No. In AP2, MPP stands for Merchant Payment Processor, a role.

items.q: Does AP2 need W3C VC 2.0 and DIDs?
items.a: No. Version 0.2 uses SD-JWT VC, OpenID4VP and the Digital Credentials API; VC 2.0 and DIDs are the wider family.

items.q: Can x402 payments travel inside AP2 mandates today?
items.a: The a2a-x402 Embedded Flow nests x402 inside AP2 CartMandate and PaymentMandate objects, which are v0.1 objects. AP2 v0.2 has no Cart mandate, so the embedding is out of step with the current version.

items.q: Is the ap2 package on PyPI Google's SDK?
items.a: No. The PyPI and npm packages named ap2 belong to unrelated third parties; Google's Python SDK is installed from the repository.
